title: Symbolic Role Polymorphism — Context Before Fixed Meaning
purpose: Replace one-symbol/one-meaning decoding with a relational model. The same object, animal, direction or geometry can perform different—even opposite—functions across biblical texts, project contexts and other traditions.
core_rule: Do not infer meaning from symbol identity alone. Interpret function from symbol × actor × relation × context × state × sequence × outcome.

formalization.better_model: function = f(symbol, actor, target, relation, context, state, sequence, outcome)
formalization.epistemic_consequence: Repeated use of the same noun is weaker evidence than repeated preservation of the same role/sequence under changing vocabulary.

obstructive: Isaiah 62 road stones are removed to prepare passage
case_matrix.lesson: Stone can support, signify, obstruct or participate in judgment/building; object identity does not fix role.

positive_or_structural: Lion heard / slain-standing Lamb seen in Revelation 5
danger_or_exclusion: Isaiah 35's protected highway is safe partly because lion/ravenous beast is absent
case_matrix.lesson: Lion can signify royal/messianic power or path danger depending literary role.

ambiguous_or_transformable: dogs at Lazarus scene do not carry a simple explicit moral taxonomy
case_matrix.lesson: Dog is not a permanent essence; the archive should encode behavior/boundary role and transformation possibility.

obstacle_or_warning: Isaiah 40 lowers mountain/hill to prepare a Way
Isaiah 14 makes ascent-to-Most-High language part of a self-exaltation warning
case_matrix.lesson: Higher is not universally holier. Altitude, center and ascent must be interpreted by function and ethical direction.

negative_or_structural: valley/depth can accompany danger, shadow or descent
restorative_or_required: Isaiah 40 raises valleys as part of preparing the Way
case_matrix.lesson: Low is not universally fallen; access sometimes requires lifting the low while lowering the high.
Door can be interface, filter, obstacle, breach site or destructible confinement depending state.

ordered: Numbers 2 differentiated camp around sacred center
transformative: Joshua 6 finite repeated circuit terminating in boundary change
case_matrix.lesson: Circularity/perimeter does not imply trap, evil or stagnation; valence follows function and outcome.

exploitative_project_form: Farm as project metaphor for extraction/control
positive_biblical_form: 1 Corinthians 3 calls the community God's field while God gives growth and workers plant/water
warning_form: Gospel tenant-farmer parable depicts abusive tenants killing the son
case_matrix.lesson: Field/Farm vocabulary itself is not the moral variable; stewardship/extraction/fruit/ownership relations are.

positive_or_structural: Tree of Life in garden center
case_matrix.warning: Network or spatial centrality does not automatically imply moral importance or divine identity; 1 Corinthians 12 makes apparently weaker members indispensable.
case_matrix.lesson: Centrality is a topology metric, not a worth metric.

reader_and_graph_rules: Every reusable symbol node should allow multiple typed roles instead of one canonical gloss.
Search/ranking should prioritize shared role and sequence over shared noun.
Opposite-valence uses are not noise; they are required evidence for meaning boundaries.
A counter-valence passage should be linked directly from positive-symbol cards.
Graph analysis should distinguish symbol nodes from function/role nodes so a high-frequency symbol cannot masquerade as one stable concept.
Machine-readable edges should prefer verbs such as supports, blocks, guards, opens, surrounds, feeds, wounds, restores or mediates rather than generic IS-A equivalence.
project_consequence: The ontology's fundamental unit becomes the relation/event, not the isolated symbol. This is consistent with the broader Potatoverse rule that coupling/relationship carries more information than naming alone.
